reviews.OriginDescription: Reviewed in the United States on March 23, 2025
reviews.Text: So I've been using this salt for a while. And though I think it's nice and salty and I like the purity of it, I swear it has little rocks in it. Every once in a while I would bite down on what felt like a grain of sand and I would get this really painful sting in my teeth... like I had a cavity or something which is what I thought was going on. I remember jumping a few times in pain it was so bad. I just figured oh well that's just how salt is, but my teeth were getting really sensitive and the pain was increasing. I was worried I was going to chip or crack a tooth as what I was biting down on did not feel like salt gains. (I do have very sensitive teeth). Anyway, I ran out of this salt a few weeks ago and just figured I would wait for my next Subscribe and Save order to bring me more. So I started using a different Himalayan salt... guess what? No crunchy little grit grains and no pain! It was definitely this salt that was causing the issue. I just cancelled my order and will be trying Crucial Four mMinerals salt. You have to order directly from their website so it's not as convenient as this, but I'm tired of eating in pain lol. I'd say if you don't have sensitive teeth this one is good. But if you do, this may not be a good fit as there is definitely grit in it.

reviews.Author: Ricardo L. Gomez Y
reviews.OriginDescription: Reviewed in the United States on April 20, 2024
reviews.Text: I purchased Redmond’s Salt mainly because I’ve been looking to switch to pure salt with no additives. I was drawn in by the promise of a natural and unrefined product, which this salt definitely is. It tastes clean and doesn't have the bitter aftertaste that some table salts can have. However, I have to admit, the price tag made me pause—it's quite expensive compared to other pure salts available on the market. I've found that you can get salt without additives for much less, almost a tenth of the price of Redmond’s, at local stores. While I appreciate the quality of Redmond’s Salt, I am not fully convinced that the higher cost is justified compared to similar products. It’s good salt, but if budget is a concern, there are other less expensive options out there that don’t compromise on purity.
